 Follow Avengers: Doomsday’s Chris Evans Reveals How Steve Rogers Has Changed Since Endgame
 Nitish Singh Tue, November 17, 2026 at 9:25 PM UTC 2 min read Add Yahoo as a preferred source to see more of our stories on Google. Photo Credit: Walt Disney Studios Motion Pictures Chris Evans is returning as Steve Rogers in Avengers: Doomsday , but the former Captain America is no longer the same man fans last saw in Avengers: Endgame . With a family to protect, Rogers now has much more at stake, which could change how he approaches the risks that once defined his life as a hero.
 Speaking to Empire , Evans explained that the biggest difference between playing Steve before and after the Endgame comes down to the stakes. The character returned to the 1940s at the end of the 2019 film to live with Peggy Carter, eventually building the quiet life he had spent so long putting aside.
 When asked whether returning to the role felt like playing a new character, Evans pointed to Steve's wife and children as the biggest difference. He explained, "Steve is at a chapter in his life where he wants to hang up the shield. He wants to find love and be a father and live a pedestrian life. I think, in his mind, he's earned that."
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement That does not mean Steve has stopped being a hero. However, according to the actor himself, having a family makes his decisions more complicated. Steve can no longer think only about saving the world. He also has people waiting for him at home.
 Who else is starring in Avengers: Doomsday with Chris Evans?
 The Russo brothers are bringing together characters from across the Marvel Cinematic Universe and the X-Men franchise for Avengers: Doomsday. Robert Downey Jr. leads the threat as Victor von Doom; it also marks his return to the MCU in a role very different from Tony Stark.
 The cast also includes Chris Hemsworth as Thor, Anthony Mackie as Sam Wilson, Sebastian Stan as Bucky Barnes, Pedro Pascal as Reed Richards, and Vanessa Kirby as Sue Storm. Florence Pugh returns as Yelena Belova, while Paul Rudd reprises his role as Scott Lang.
 Several familiar X-Men characters are also joining the film. Patrick Stewart returns as Professor X, Ian McKellen as Magneto, James Marsden as Cyclops, Rebecca Romijn as Mystique, Alan Cumming as Nightcrawler, and Kelsey Grammer as Beast.
 Advertisement Advertisement Other returning MCU stars include Hayley Atwell as Peggy Carter, Tom Hiddleston as Loki, Letitia Wright as Shuri, Simu Liu as Shang-Chi, and Channing Tatum as Gambit.
